title: checkout-api 5xx after v2.30.1 deploy
summary: checkout-api failed 4.8% of requests after dep-0016 (v2.30.1) switched cart serialization to orjson, which cannot encode Decimal prices on discounted carts. Rolled back to v2.30.0.

timeline.text: Alert: checkout-api error rate 4.8% (threshold 1%). Incident opened.
Leila sees 'TypeError: Decimal is not JSON serializable' in checkout-api logs, starting right after dep-0016.
Roll back dep-0016 rather than hotfix: every cart with a discount code hits the error.
Rolled checkout-api back to v2.30.0.
Error rate under 0.2% for 8 minutes. Resolved.

postmortem.title: checkout-api errors from orjson cart serialization
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For 19 minutes checkout-api failed 4.8% of requests after dep-0016 (v2.30.1) switched cart serialization to orjson.

## Impact
Shoppers using a discount code could not check out. Nobody was charged twice.

## Root cause
Commit 1005fd5 by Ben Carter serialized line item prices with orjson, which does not encode Decimal. Carts without discounts carry float prices and worked, so the unit tests passed.

## Resolution
Leila Ahmadi rolled checkout-api back to v2.30.0.

## Follow-ups
- Add a discounted cart to the checkout-api contract tests.
- Represent money as integer cents everywhere in checkout-api.
postmortem.author: leila

title: Card payments timing out at the primary acquirer
summary: Northbank, the primary acquirer, slowed to 4,200 ms p99 and timed out charges; checkout-api errors reached 6.1%. Switched card traffic to Meridian with the runbook until Northbank recovered.

timeline.text: Alert: acquirer-gateway p99 latency 4,200 ms (threshold 2500 ms).
Alert: checkout-api error rate 6.1%. Sev1 opened.
acquirer-gateway itself is healthy; timeouts are on the Northbank connection only. No Kestrel Pay change in the last 6 hours.
Northbank's status page confirms degraded authorization latency.
Ran 'Route card traffic to the backup acquirer': primary_acquirer set to meridian.
Authorizations succeeding through Meridian; checkout-api error rate 0.4%.
Northbank reports recovery; primary_acquirer switched back to northbank.
Resolved.

postmortem.title: Northbank authorization latency
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Northbank, our primary acquirer, degraded for about 90 minutes. Charges timed out until we routed traffic to Meridian 14 minutes in.

## Impact
6.1% of checkouts failed for 20 minutes. Meridian costs 0.04% more per transaction while it carries traffic.

## Root cause
External: Northbank authorization latency. No Kestrel Pay change was involved.

## Resolution
Kwame Mensah ran "Route card traffic to the backup acquirer" and switched back once Northbank recovered.

## Follow-ups
- Alert on acquirer latency before checkout errors, so the switch happens sooner.
- Ask Northbank for status page webhooks.
postmortem.author: kwame

title: Webhook retry storm after max_retries raised to 30
summary: Nina Johansson raised webhooks-svc max_retries from 8 to 30 (cfg-0004). Deliveries to failing merchant endpoints were retried far more often, delivery p99 hit 9,800 ms and kafka disk reached 88%. Restored 8 and drained the backlog.

timeline.text: Alert: webhooks-svc delivery p99 9,800 ms (threshold 5000 ms).
Alert: kafka saturation 88%; the webhook retry topic is growing fast.
Retries per delivery up 4x since cfg-0004 raised max_retries to 30, 12 minutes before the first alert.
Set webhooks-svc max_retries back to 8.
Ran 'Scale webhooks-svc and drain the delivery backlog'.
Consumer lag under a minute; kafka disk back to 61%. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Raising webhook retries flooded kafka
postmortem.body:
## Summary
cfg-0004 raised webhooks-svc max_retries from 8 to 30. Within 12 minutes retries to dead merchant endpoints dominated delivery and filled the retry topic.

## Impact
Webhook delivery to every merchant slowed to 9,800 ms p99 for about an hour. Kafka disk reached 88%, close to affecting payment events.

## Root cause
Nina Johansson raised retries to help one merchant with a flaky endpoint. Retries are per delivery, so every failing endpoint got the same treatment.

## Resolution
Lucy Evans restored max_retries to 8 and drained the backlog with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Per-merchant retry budgets instead of one global setting.
- Separate disk quota for the webhook retry topic.
postmortem.author: lucy

title: Merchant search failing after Elasticsearch upgrade
summary: dep-0047 upgraded search-index to v4.6.7; the new nodes could not read the old shard allocation and the cluster went red. search-api failed 12% of queries. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: search-api error rate 12% (threshold 2%).
search-index cluster health red; 14 primary shards unassigned since dep-0047.
Roll back the upgrade: tier 3, but merchants cannot find orders in the dashboard.
Rolled search-index back to v4.6.6; shards reallocating.
Cluster green, search working. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Elasticsearch upgrade left shards unassigned
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Merchant order search was down for 62 minutes after dep-0047 upgraded search-index to v4.6.7.

## Impact
Dashboard search failed for all merchants (12% of queries). Payments were not affected.

## Root cause
Commit b457208 by Kai Nakamura switched to the desired-balance allocator in the same change as the version upgrade. Mixed-version nodes could not agree on allocation.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v4.6.6; shards reallocated in about 25 minutes.

## Follow-ups
- Upgrade versions and change allocator settings in separate deploys.
- Rehearse search-index upgrades on the staging snapshot.
postmortem.author: lucy

title: Sessions dropped after redis-cache maxmemory cut to 4gb
summary: Lukas Becker lowered redis-cache maxmemory from 8gb to 4gb (cfg-0006) to make room on the host. Redis evicted session and idempotency keys; auth-svc errors reached 9.5% and shoppers were logged out mid-checkout. Restored 8gb with the runbook.

timeline.text: Alert: redis-cache memory 99% of maxmemory.
Alert: auth-svc error rate 9.5%. Sev1 opened.
Alert: checkout-api error rate 3.2%.
evicted_keys climbing by 40k/s. cfg-0006 cut maxmemory to 4gb 14 minutes before the first alert.
Ran 'Restore redis-cache maxmemory and eviction policy': maxmemory back to 8gb.
Evictions stopped; auth-svc owners confirm sessions are stable.
auth-svc and checkout-api error rates normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: redis-cache maxmemory cut evicted sessions
postmortem.body:
## Summary
cfg-0006 lowered redis-cache maxmemory from 8gb to 4gb. Redis started evicting keys at once, including sessions and idempotency keys.

## Impact
For 33 minutes auth-svc failed 9.5% of requests and checkout-api 3.2%. Merchants were logged out of the dashboard; some shoppers had to restart checkout.

## Root cause
Lukas Becker reduced memory to fit a second Redis on the same host. Everything that uses redis-cache shares one keyspace, so the eviction policy cannot protect sessions.

## Resolution
Noor Haddad restored maxmemory to 8gb with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Move sessions to their own Redis with noeviction.
- Alert on evicted_keys, not just memory.
postmortem.author: noor

title: payments-svc rejecting retries as duplicates after v3.16.5
summary: dep-0065 (v3.16.5) derived idempotency keys from the cart id alone, so legitimate retries after a soft decline were rejected as duplicates. payments-svc errors reached 5.5%. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-svc error rate 5.5%. Sev1 opened.
Alert: checkout-api error rate 4.9%.
Errors are 409 duplicate_request on second attempts; the idempotency key format changed in dep-0065.
Rolled payments-svc back to v3.16.4.
Retries succeeding. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Idempotency keys collided on retries
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For 18 minutes payments-svc rejected 5.5% of charges as duplicates after dep-0065 (v3.16.5) changed how idempotency keys are built.

## Impact
Shoppers whose first attempt was soft-declined could not retry with another card. checkout-api errors reached 4.9%.

## Root cause
Commit f21bd41 by Oliver Hughes keyed idempotency on the cart id only. A retry with a new card is a new payment attempt and needs its own key.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v3.16.4.

## Follow-ups
- Idempotency key = cart id + attempt number.
- Test: soft decline then retry with a different card.
postmortem.author: hana

title: Receipt emails failing at the email provider
summary: Postmark returned 503 on 38% of sends for 47 minutes. No Kestrel Pay change; queued receipts were sent once the provider recovered.

timeline.text: Alert: notifications-svc error rate 38%.
503s from Postmark only; SMS through Twilio unaffected. Postmark's status page shows an outage.
Wait it out: receipts stay queued in kafka and are retried, nothing is lost.
Postmark recovered; backlog sent. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Postmark outage delayed receipts
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Receipt emails were delayed for 47 minutes while Postmark was down.

## Impact
Shoppers got receipts late. No emails were lost.

## Root cause
External: Postmark outage.

## Resolution
Grace Liu confirmed receipts were buffered in kafka and waited for recovery.

## Follow-ups
- Evaluate a second email provider.
postmortem.author: grace

title: inventory-svc slow after a migration dropped the reservations index
summary: dep-0092 (v3.14.0) ran a migration that dropped idx_reservations_sku_expires as unused. Reservation lookups became sequential scans; inventory-svc p99 hit 1,850 ms and checkout-api 2,900 ms. Recreated the index concurrently.

timeline.text: Alert: inventory-svc p99 latency 1,850 ms (threshold 200 ms).
Alert: checkout-api p99 latency 2,900 ms.
inventory-db CPU at 96%; pg_stat_activity shows sequential scans on stock_reservations.
The migration in dep-0092 dropped idx_reservations_sku_expires 17 minutes before the first alert.
Do not roll back a database deploy (policy no-database-rollback); recreate the index instead.
Ran 'Kill runaway queries and restore the inventory-db index'.
Index rebuilt; inventory-svc p99 back to 22 ms. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Dropping an 'unused' index made inventory-db scan
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0092 (v3.14.0) dropped idx_reservations_sku_expires. inventory-db fell back to sequential scans and inventory-svc p99 reached 1,850 ms.

## Impact
Checkouts were slow for 52 minutes (checkout-api p99 2,900 ms). No failed payments.

## Root cause
Commit 5469c14 by Yuki Tanaka dropped indexes reported unused by pg_stat_user_indexes on a replica, where the reservation expiry query never runs.

## Resolution
Amara Okafor cancelled the runaway queries and recreated the index concurrently with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Check index usage on the primary before dropping.
- Review inventory-db migrations with the checkout team.
postmortem.author: amara

title: Checkout failing: payments-db connection pool exhausted
summary: Tomás Ortega lowered payments-db max_pool_size from 200 to 120 (cfg-0010) to cut idle connections. At peak payments-svc could not get a connection, charges timed out and checkout-api errors reached 7.9%. Failing over did not help; raising max_pool_size back to 200 and restarting payments-svc did.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-db pool saturation 100%.
Alert: checkout-api error rate 7.9%. Sev1 opened.
payments-svc logs 'timeout acquiring connection'; payments-db CPU is only 35%.
Suspect a sick primary: connections pinned at the pool limit although queries are fast.
Ran 'Fail over payments-db to the standby'.
Failover did not help: the standby has the same max_pool_size and filled up within a minute.
cfg-0010 lowered max_pool_size from 200 to 120 13 minutes before the first alert.
Raised max_pool_size back to 200 and restarted payments-svc pod by pod.
Charges succeeding; checkout-api errors under 1% for 10 minutes. Resolved.

postmortem.title: payments-db pool cut to 120 exhausted connections at peak
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For 53 minutes checkout failed for most shoppers. payments-db's server-side pool was lowered from 200 to 120 (cfg-0010); at peak payments-svc needs about 160 connections.

## Impact
7.9% of checkouts failed. Charges that timed out were never captured, so nobody was charged twice.

## Root cause
Tomás Ortega lowered the pool off-peak to cut idle connections. Config changes to payments-db skip the deploy pipeline and had no review. Every payments-svc pod shares the one pool, so the limit is hit everywhere at once.

## What did not work
Failing over to the standby (minute 21) cost 8 minutes: the standby has the same pool config.

## Resolution
Hana Kim raised max_pool_size back to 200 and restarted payments-svc so every pod reconnected.

## Follow-ups
- Alert on pool saturation above 80%, before checkout fails.
- Require a payments review for changes to services/payments-db/config.yaml.
- Write the runbook "Raise pool + restart payments-svc".
postmortem.author: hana

title: fraud-svc latency from a heavier model in v3.28.8
summary: dep-0110 (v3.28.8) shipped a fraud model with three times the features; scoring p99 rose to 410 ms and payments-svc p99 to 1,300 ms. Switched to rules-only scoring, rolled back, then restored model scoring.

timeline.text: Alert: fraud-svc p99 latency 410 ms (threshold 150 ms).
Alert: payments-svc p99 latency 1,300 ms.
Model inference time tripled after dep-0110 loaded the new model.
Ran 'Switch fraud scoring to the rules-only fallback'.
payments-svc latency normal on rules-only scoring.
Rolled fraud-svc back to v3.28.7.
Set scoring_mode back to model, on the old model.
Model scoring healthy. Resolved.

postmortem.title: New fraud model too slow for the charge path
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0110 (v3.28.8) loaded a larger fraud model. Scoring p99 reached 410 ms, which pushed payments-svc p99 to 1,300 ms.

## Impact
Slow checkouts for 14 minutes, then 17 minutes of rules-only scoring with more manual reviews.

## Root cause
Commit 48b124e by Arjun Mehta shipped a model benchmarked on a GPU box; production scores on CPU.

## Resolution
Fatima Bello switched to rules-only scoring with the runbook, rolled back, then restored model scoring.

## Follow-ups
- Latency budget check for models in CI, on production hardware.
postmortem.author: fatima

title: checkout-api failing every checkout after v2.32.1
summary: dep-0115 (v2.32.1) pointed checkout-api's pricing client at a pricing-svc v2 endpoint that did not exist yet; every price lookup returned 404 and checkout-api failed 11.3% of requests. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: checkout-api error rate 11.3%. Sev1 opened: checkout is effectively down.
checkout-api logs 404 from pricing-svc on /v2/quotes; pricing-svc itself is healthy.
dep-0115 went out 14 minutes before the alert and changed the pricing client.
Roll back dep-0115: pricing-svc has not shipped v2 yet.
Rolled checkout-api back to v2.32.0.
Checkout success rate back to normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: checkout-api called a pricing-svc endpoint that did not exist yet
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Checkout failed for 14 minutes (11.3% errors) because dep-0115 called pricing-svc's v2 quote endpoint before pricing-svc shipped it.

## Impact
Most checkouts failed during the window; shoppers saw "unable to price cart".

## Root cause
Commit a12104f by Mateo Silva assumed the pricing-svc v2 rollout had finished. The two changes were coordinated in chat, not in the deploy pipeline.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v2.32.0.

## Follow-ups
- Contract test between checkout-api and pricing-svc in CI.
- Put client switches to new upstream endpoints behind a flag.
postmortem.author: ben

title: api-gateway 504s after upstream timeout cut to 800 ms
summary: Dev Malhotra lowered api-gateway upstream_timeout_ms from 3000 to 800 (cfg-0017). checkout-api calls that wait on card authorization take up to 2 s, so the gateway cut them off with 504s (3.9% of requests). Restored 3000 ms.

timeline.text: Alert: api-gateway error rate 3.9%.
All errors are 504 on the checkout-api upstream; checkout-api logs show those requests completing after the client left.
cfg-0017 set upstream_timeout_ms to 800 8 minutes before the alert.
Ran 'Restore api-gateway upstream timeouts'.
504s stopped. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Gateway timeout shorter than card authorization
postmortem.body:
## Summary
cfg-0017 lowered api-gateway upstream_timeout_ms from 3000 to 800. Checkouts that wait on the acquirer take up to 2 seconds and were cut off.

## Impact
3.9% of API calls returned 504 for 21 minutes. Some charges completed after the shopper saw an error.

## Root cause
Dev Malhotra tuned the timeout for user-api and search-api; the setting is global.

## Resolution
Jin Park restored 3000 ms with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Per-route upstream timeouts.
- Reconcile charges that completed after a 504.
postmortem.author: jin

title: ledger-svc stopped consuming payment events after v1.27.4
summary: dep-0144 (v1.27.4) added a strict schema check that rejected events from an older producer; the consumer stopped at the first one and ledger lag reached 54,000 ms. Rolled back and replayed from the stuck offset.

timeline.text: Alert: ledger-svc event processing lag 54,000 ms.
Consumer stuck on one offset; that event has schema version 3 and the new check only accepts 4.
The check came in dep-0144, deployed 9 minutes before the alert.
Rolled ledger-svc back to v1.27.3.
Ran 'Replay missed payment events into ledger-svc' from the stuck offset.
Balance check job: merchant balances match payments-db totals.
Lag back to zero. Resolved.

postmortem.title: ledger-svc consumer blocked on an old event schema
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0144 (v1.27.4) made ledger-svc reject payment events with schema version 3. The consumer stopped and ledger lag reached 54,000 ms.

## Impact
Merchant balances were stale for 74 minutes; payouts-svc held the 08:00 payout run.

## Root cause
Commit 03277a7 by Inês Costa assumed every producer was on schema version 4. payouts-svc still emits version 3 for adjustments.

## Resolution
Inês Costa rolled back and replayed from the stuck offset.

## Follow-ups
- Dead-letter unknown schema versions instead of stopping the consumer.
- A second ledger-svc reviewer: only Inês Costa knows the consumer code.
postmortem.author: ines

title: auth-svc rejecting tokens: signing key expired
summary: The auth-svc token signing key reached its 90-day expiry; new tokens failed validation at api-gateway and 14% of API calls returned 401. Rotated to the next key with the runbook.

timeline.text: Alert: auth-svc error rate 22%. Sev1 opened.
Alert: api-gateway error rate 14%.
Tokens signed after 23:00 UTC fail validation; the active signing key expired at 23:00.
Ran 'Rotate the auth-svc token signing key'.
New tokens validate; 401s back to baseline. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Expired signing key, rotation not automated
postmortem.body:
## Summary
The auth-svc signing key expired at 23:00 UTC. For 26 minutes newly issued tokens failed validation.

## Impact
14% of API calls failed with 401; merchants could not log in to the dashboard.

## Root cause
Key rotation every 90 days is manual and the calendar reminder went to someone who left.

## Resolution
Arjun Mehta activated the next key with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Rotate keys automatically 7 days before expiry.
- Alert 14 days before any signing key expires.
postmortem.author: arjun

title: Kafka brokers near full disk after retention raised to 720 h
summary: Noor Haddad raised kafka retention_hours from 168 to 720 (cfg-0022) for an analytics backfill. Local disk on two brokers reached 95%, producers slowed and ledger-svc lag hit 21,000 ms. Restored 168 h and moved partitions off the full brokers.

timeline.text: Alert: kafka disk 95%.
Alert: ledger-svc event processing lag 21,000 ms.
Brokers 2 and 4 above 90% disk; segment deletion stopped after cfg-0022 raised retention to 720 h.
Set retention_hours back to 168; old segments are deleting.
Ran 'Move partitions off a full Kafka broker' for brokers 2 and 4.
Brokers under 70% disk, ledger-svc lag zero. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Kafka retention raised without disk headroom
postmortem.body:
## Summary
cfg-0022 raised retention_hours from 168 to 720. Brokers stopped deleting segments and two filled to 95%.

## Impact
Produce latency rose for every service; ledger-svc lag reached 21,000 ms. No events were lost.

## Root cause
Noor Haddad raised retention for a one-off analytics backfill that should have read from tiered storage in object-store.

## Resolution
Lukas Becker restored 168 h and reassigned partitions with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Backfills read from tiered storage, never from longer broker retention.
- Disk alert per broker at 75%.
postmortem.author: lukas

title: Edge WAF blocking legitimate checkouts after rule update
summary: dep-0177 (v1.9.2) shipped a WAF rule set that matched the mobile SDK's base64 payment payload as SQL injection; 18% of requests got 403. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: edge error rate 18%. Sev1 opened.
403s from the WAF on /v1/checkout, mobile SDK traffic only.
Rule update in dep-0177, 9 minutes before the alert.
Rolled edge back to v1.9.1.
403s gone. Resolved.

postmortem.title: WAF paranoia level 2 blocked mobile checkouts
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0177 (v1.9.2) raised the WAF paranoia level. Mobile SDK checkout payloads matched SQL injection rules and got 403.

## Impact
18% of requests, all mobile checkouts, failed for 12 minutes.

## Root cause
Commit 561886a by Sofia Rossi was tested against web traffic only.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v1.9.1.

## Follow-ups
- Run new WAF rules in detect mode for a week before block.
postmortem.author: sofia

title: Charges timing out after acquirer read timeout cut to 1000 ms
summary: Kwame Mensah lowered acquirer-gateway read_timeout_ms from 2500 to 1000 (cfg-0025). Slow but valid authorizations were abandoned and payments-svc errors reached 3.4%. Switching acquirers did not help; restoring 2500 ms did.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-svc error rate 3.4%.
acquirer-gateway reports read timeouts on Northbank. Looks like the Northbank outage in INC-012.
Ran 'Route card traffic to the backup acquirer'.
Same timeouts on Meridian, so the problem is on our side.
cfg-0025 lowered read_timeout_ms to 1000 15 minutes before the alert; p95 authorization time is 1.4 s.
Set read_timeout_ms back to 2500.
Switched primary_acquirer back to northbank.
payments-svc errors normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Acquirer read timeout below real authorization time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
cfg-0025 lowered acquirer-gateway read_timeout_ms from 2500 to 1000. About 1 in 30 authorizations takes longer than that and was abandoned.

## Impact
3.4% of charges failed for 34 minutes.

## Root cause
Kwame Mensah lowered the timeout to fail fast during acquirer outages like INC-012, without checking the authorization time distribution.

## What did not work
The acquirer switch runbook (minute 12): it fixes acquirer outages, not our own timeouts.

## Resolution
Kwame Mensah restored 2500 ms and switched back to Northbank.

## Follow-ups
- Timeout changes on acquirer-gateway need the p99 authorization time in the review.
postmortem.author: kwame

title: Merchant payouts batch failed after v1.19.18
summary: dep-0196 (v1.19.18) sent payout amounts as decimal strings to the bank file builder, which expects integer cents; every payout in the 16:00 batch failed. Rolled back and re-ran the batch before the bank cutoff.

timeline.text: Alert: payouts-svc error rate 100%: the 16:00 UTC payout batch failed.
Bank file validation error: amount '1250.00' is not an integer.
Amount formatting changed in dep-0196.
Rolled payouts-svc back to v1.19.17.
Re-ran the 16:00 batch; 1,184 payouts accepted.
Payouts sent before the bank's 17:00 cutoff. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Payout amounts formatted as decimals
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0196 (v1.19.18) formatted payout amounts as decimal strings. The bank file builder rejected the whole 16:00 batch.

## Impact
Payouts were 24 minutes late but made the bank cutoff. No merchant was paid twice.

## Root cause
Commit 8e9500c by Raj Iyer reused a money helper meant for display.

## Resolution
Inês Costa rolled back and re-ran the batch.

## Follow-ups
- Validate the bank file in CI against the bank's schema.
postmortem.author: ines

title: Webhook signatures invalid after v2.34.1
summary: dep-0197 (v2.34.1) re-serialized webhook bodies after signing them, so merchant signature checks failed on 27% of deliveries. Rolled back; failed deliveries were retried.

timeline.text: Alert: webhooks-svc delivery error rate 27%.
Merchants return 401 invalid signature; since dep-0197 the signed bytes differ from the sent bytes.
Rolled webhooks-svc back to v2.34.0.
Retries delivered; error rate normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Pretty-printing broke webhook signatures
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0197 (v2.34.1) pretty-printed webhook bodies after computing the signature. Merchants verifying signatures rejected 27% of deliveries.

## Impact
Webhooks to merchants that verify signatures failed for 31 minutes; all were redelivered.

## Root cause
Commit 913c624 by Omar Farouk changed serialization in the sender, not the signer.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v2.34.0.

## Follow-ups
- Sign the exact bytes sent; test with a real verifier.
postmortem.author: kai

title: search-index disk flood-stage watermark reached
summary: search-index data nodes passed the flood-stage disk watermark (97%) and indices went read-only; search-api failed 8% of queries. Deleted expired indices and cleared the read-only block.

timeline.text: Alert: search-index disk 97%.
Alert: search-api error rate 8%.
Indices are read-only (flood-stage watermark). The 13-month retention job has not run for 3 weeks.
Deleted indices older than 13 months and removed the read-only block.
Disk at 71%, search working. Resolved.

postmortem.title: search-index retention job silently stopped
postmortem.body:
## Summary
search-index disks filled to 97% and Elasticsearch made indices read-only, so new transactions could not be indexed and search-api failed 8% of queries.

## Impact
Merchant search was degraded for 40 minutes. Tier 3; no payment impact.

## Root cause
The nightly retention job had been failing for three weeks after its credentials rotated. Nobody was alerted.

## Resolution
Lucy Evans deleted expired indices by hand and cleared the read-only block.

## Follow-ups
- Alert when the retention job has not succeeded for 2 days.
- Disk alert at 80%, well before the flood-stage watermark.
postmortem.author: lucy

title: payments-db pool exhausted again after max_pool_size cut to 100
summary: Same failure as INC-019. Oliver Hughes lowered payments-db max_pool_size from 200 to 100 (cfg-0036) to match a pgbouncer default; checkout-api errors reached 9.4%. A checkout-api deploy (dep-0225) 5 minutes before the alert looked suspicious but was unrelated. Raised the pool and restarted payments-svc.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-db pool saturation 99%.
Alert: checkout-api error rate 9.4%. Sev1 opened.
Alert: payments-svc p99 latency 2,600 ms.
checkout-api deployed v2.41.0 (dep-0225) just before the alert, but its errors are timeouts from payments-svc, not checkout code.
payments-svc waits on connections at the pool limit, same signature as INC-019. cfg-0036 lowered max_pool_size to 100.
Skip the failover (it did not help in INC-019); go straight to the pool runbook.
Ran 'Raise pool + restart payments-svc': max_pool_size back to 200.
Checkout errors under 1% for 10 minutes. Resolved.

postmortem.title: payments-db pool exhaustion, second time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
cfg-0036 lowered payments-db max_pool_size from 200 to 100, and checkout failed exactly as in INC-019. Resolved in 27 minutes with the runbook written after INC-019.

## Impact
9.4% of checkouts failed for about 15 minutes.

## Root cause
Oliver Hughes aligned max_pool_size with a pgbouncer default. The review required after INC-019 was not enforced in tooling.

## Red herring
checkout-api v2.41.0 (dep-0225) shipped 5 minutes before the alert. It was the most recent deploy, but checkout's errors were payments-svc timeouts two hops downstream.

## Resolution
Priya Raman ran "Raise pool + restart payments-svc" without trying the failover first.

## Follow-ups
- CODEOWNERS review on services/payments-db/config.yaml, enforced in CI.
- Pool saturation alert at 80% (from INC-019, still open).
postmortem.author: priya

title: False fraud declines after block threshold lowered to 0.6
summary: Arjun Mehta lowered fraud-svc block_threshold from 0.85 to 0.6 (cfg-0038), meaning to change the review queue. About one charge in fifteen was blocked as fraud and payments-svc declines reached 6.6%. Restored 0.85.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-svc error rate 6.6% (fraud declines).
Declines are fraud_blocked with scores between 0.6 and 0.85; the model's score distribution is unchanged.
cfg-0038 set block_threshold to 0.6 12 minutes before the alert; review_threshold is also 0.6.
Set block_threshold back to 0.85.
Decline rate normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Block threshold set to the review threshold
postmortem.body:
## Summary
cfg-0038 lowered fraud-svc block_threshold from 0.85 to 0.6. Charges that should have gone to manual review were declined.

## Impact
6.6% of charges were declined as fraud for 20 minutes.

## Root cause
Arjun Mehta edited block_threshold instead of review_threshold; the two keys sit next to each other.

## Resolution
Chloé Martin restored 0.85.

## Follow-ups
- Validate block_threshold > review_threshold + 0.1.
postmortem.author: chloe

title: checkout-api p99 latency over 3 s after v2.41.1
summary: dep-0239 (v2.41.1) added a synchronous stock re-check per cart line; large carts made one inventory-svc call per line in sequence and checkout-api p99 reached 3,100 ms. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: checkout-api p99 latency 3,100 ms (threshold 800 ms).
Traces show one inventory-svc call per cart line, in sequence; inventory-svc answers each in 15 ms.
The per-line re-check came in dep-0239, deployed 16 minutes before the alert.
Rolled checkout-api back to v2.41.0.
p99 back to 240 ms. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Per-line stock re-check made large carts slow
postmortem.body:
## Summary
checkout-api p99 latency reached 3,100 ms for 17 minutes after dep-0239 (v2.41.1) re-checked stock once per cart line.

## Impact
Carts with more than 20 lines took over 3 seconds to start payment; some shoppers abandoned.

## Root cause
Commit 56ef0b4 by Leila Ahmadi called inventory-svc in a loop. inventory-svc already has a batch endpoint.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v2.41.0.

## Follow-ups
- Use the inventory-svc batch reservation check.
- Add a 50-line cart to the checkout-api load test.
postmortem.author: amara

title: redis-cache primary unreachable
summary: The redis-cache primary host lost its network interface; every Redis call failed, auth-svc errors hit 31% and checkout-api, webhooks-svc and pricing-svc degraded. Promoted the replica with the runbook.

timeline.text: Alert: redis-cache error rate 100%. Sev1 opened.
Alert: auth-svc error rate 31%.
Primary does not answer PING from two hosts; the replica is healthy. No recent change on redis-cache.
Ran 'Promote the redis-cache replica'.
Restarted auth-svc, checkout-api and webhooks-svc to drop the old primary address.
All services healthy. Resolved.

postmortem.title: redis-cache primary host network failure
postmortem.body:
## Summary
The redis-cache primary became unreachable after a host NIC failure. Everything that uses Redis degraded until the replica was promoted.

## Impact
auth-svc failed 31% of requests for 24 minutes; checkout-api, webhooks-svc and pricing-svc were degraded.

## Root cause
Hardware: NIC failure on the primary host. Sentinel did not fail over because two sentinels ran on that host.

## Resolution
Dev Malhotra promoted the replica by hand and restarted clients that pin the primary address.

## Follow-ups
- Spread sentinels across three hosts.
- Clients resolve the primary through sentinel, not a fixed address.
postmortem.author: dev

title: Kafka rejecting payment events after schema-registry v2.29.12
summary: dep-0259 (v2.29.12) changed schema-registry's subject naming, so brokers could not find the schema for payment-events and rejected every produced record. payments-svc errors reached 4.1%. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-svc error rate 4.1%. Sev1 opened.
Alert: checkout-api error rate 2.7%.
payments-svc produce calls fail with INVALID_RECORD: no schema for subject payment-events-value.
schema-registry v2.29.12 (dep-0259) changed the subject naming strategy 7 minutes before the alert.
Rolled schema-registry back to v2.29.11.
Produces succeeding. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Subject naming change broke broker-side schema validation
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0259 (v2.29.12) switched schema-registry to RecordNameStrategy. Brokers validate every record against the registry and could no longer find the payment-events schema.

## Impact
payments-svc failed 4.1% of charges and checkout-api 2.7% for 22 minutes: charges are rolled back when the payment event cannot be produced.

## Root cause
Commit 52f571a by Dev Malhotra was tested with clients only. Kafka depends on schema-registry for every produced record, not only for new schemas.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v2.29.11.

## Follow-ups
- Staging test that produces through brokers with validation on.
postmortem.author: dev

title: Reconciliation reporting false mismatches after v1.10.0
summary: dep-0269 (v1.10.0) compared settlement amounts in the acquirer's currency against ledger amounts in the merchant's currency; 14% of lines were flagged as mismatched. Rolled back and re-ran the job.

timeline.text: Alert: reconciliation-job mismatch rate 14% (threshold 0.5%).
Every flagged line is a cross-currency charge.
Amount comparison changed in dep-0269.
Rolled reconciliation-job back to v1.9.3 and re-ran last night's batch.
Mismatch rate 0.02%. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Reconciliation compared amounts in different currencies
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0269 (v1.10.0) compared settlement and ledger amounts in different currencies, flagging 14% of lines.

## Impact
The finance team got a false mismatch report; no money moved.

## Root cause
Commit 12e3f1d by Elena Petrova used the presentment amount; settlement files carry the settlement currency.

## Resolution
Inês Costa rolled back and re-ran the batch.

## Follow-ups
- Cross-currency fixtures in the reconciliation tests.
postmortem.author: ines

title: Northbank declining charges with system errors
summary: Northbank returned system errors (response code 96) on 35% of authorizations and checkout-api errors hit 8.8%. Same pattern as INC-012: switched to Meridian with the runbook within 9 minutes.

timeline.text: Alert: acquirer-gateway error rate 35%.
Alert: checkout-api error rate 8.8%. Sev1 opened.
Response code 96 (system malfunction) from Northbank only; Meridian test charges pass. Same pattern as INC-012.
Ran 'Route card traffic to the backup acquirer'.
Checkout error rate back to 0.3% on Meridian.
Northbank confirmed a fix; primary_acquirer switched back to northbank.
Resolved.

postmortem.title: Northbank system errors, second outage
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Northbank failed 35% of authorizations with response code 96 for about an hour. Second Northbank outage after INC-012.

## Impact
8.8% of checkouts failed for 12 minutes, until traffic moved to Meridian.

## Root cause
External: a Northbank processor fault.

## Resolution
Priya Raman ran "Route card traffic to the backup acquirer" 9 minutes in, faster than INC-012 because the runbook was known.

## Follow-ups
- Automate the acquirer switch when one acquirer's error rate passes 20%.
postmortem.author: priya

title: inventory-svc N+1 queries after v4.2.0
summary: dep-0283 (v4.2.0) loaded reservations one SKU at a time instead of in one query; inventory-svc p99 reached 920 ms and inventory-db saturation 93%. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: inventory-svc p99 latency 920 ms.
Alert: inventory-db saturation 93%.
Queries per request up from 2 to about 40 since dep-0283.
Not the missing index from INC-018: indexes are intact, there are just many more queries.
Rolled inventory-svc back to v4.1.9.
p99 back to 20 ms. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Repository layer issued one query per SKU
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0283 (v4.2.0) moved reservation loading to a repository layer that queries per SKU. inventory-svc p99 reached 920 ms.

## Impact
Slow checkouts for 18 minutes; no failures.

## Root cause
Commit e09deb2 by Yuki Tanaka: the new repository layer lacks a batch load method.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v4.1.9.

## Follow-ups
- Query count assertion in the inventory-svc integration tests.
postmortem.author: ben

title: user-api errors on merchant profiles after v3.29.0
summary: dep-0292 (v3.29.0) made merchant legal_name required, but merchants created before 2024 have none; 6% of profile reads failed. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: user-api error rate 6%.
ValidationError: legal_name is required; only older merchants are affected.
Rolled user-api back to v3.28.0.
Resolved.

postmortem.title: Required field missing on old merchant records
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0292 (v3.29.0) required legal_name on every merchant profile; older merchants do not have one.

## Impact
6% of profile reads failed for 18 minutes. The dashboard showed an error for those merchants.

## Root cause
Commit bc0a87c by Kai Nakamura was tested on recent fixtures only.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v3.28.0.

## Follow-ups
- Backfill legal_name before making it required.
postmortem.author: nina

title: Kafka leader elections flapping after controller upgrade
summary: dep-0312 upgraded kafka-controller to v4.16.2 one node at a time, but one node came back with a stale voters list; partition leaders kept moving and kafka produce errors reached 3%. Restored the quorum with the runbook.

timeline.text: Alert: kafka produce error rate 3%.
Alert: payments-svc p99 latency 900 ms.
NOT_LEADER_OR_FOLLOWER errors; partition leaders change every few seconds.
Controller 3, restarted by dep-0312, came back with the old voters list; two controllers both claim leadership.
Ran 'Restore the KRaft controller quorum'.
One active controller, no under-replicated partitions. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Stale voters list split the KRaft quorum
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0312 upgraded the KRaft controllers to v4.16.2. One node restarted with an outdated voters list and the quorum split.

## Impact
Kafka produce errors reached 3% for 39 minutes; payments-svc p99 rose to 900 ms. Every service on kafka was affected.

## Root cause
Commit 24e6b92 by Noor Haddad set the new bootstrap setting but left the old static voters list on controller 3.

## Resolution
Lukas Becker restored the quorum with the runbook. A database-style rollback was not possible mid-upgrade.

## Follow-ups
- Render controller config from one template.
- Quorum health check between each node restart in the upgrade script.
postmortem.author: lukas

title: checkout-api errors on guest carts after v2.43.3
summary: dep-0320 (v2.43.3) offered saved cards on every cart; guest carts have no customer id and checkout-api raised KeyError on 3.6% of requests. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: checkout-api error rate 3.6%.
"KeyError: 'customer_id'" in the payment step; only guest carts are affected.
dep-0320 by Ben changed the saved-cards query 9 minutes before the alert.
Roll back instead of turning off enable_saved_cards: the flag also gates signed-in shoppers.
Rolled checkout-api back to v2.43.2.
Errors gone. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Saved cards broke guest checkout
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Guest checkouts failed for 20 minutes (3.6% of requests) after dep-0320 (v2.43.3) offered saved cards on every cart.

## Impact
Guest shoppers, about a third of checkout traffic, could not pay.

## Root cause
Commit fd564b9 by Ben Carter read customer_id from every cart; guest carts do not have one. Tests only used signed-in fixtures.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v2.43.2.

## Follow-ups
- Guest cart fixture in the checkout-api test suite.
- Split enable_saved_cards into per-audience flags.
postmortem.author: yuki

title: Third payments-db pool exhaustion: max_pool_size cut to 90
summary: Kwame Mensah lowered payments-db max_pool_size from 200 to 90 (cfg-0050) to free connections for reconciliation-job. checkout-api errors reached 8.6%, the third time after INC-019 and INC-031. Ignored a checkout-api deploy that landed 7 minutes earlier, raised the pool back to 200 and restarted payments-svc.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-db pool saturation 100%.
Alert: checkout-api error rate 8.6%. Sev1 opened.
Latest deploy is checkout-api v2.44.1 by Mateo Silva, but checkout's errors are payments-svc timeouts.
cfg-0050 lowered max_pool_size to 90. Same cause as INC-019 and INC-031.
Ran 'Raise pool + restart payments-svc': max_pool_size back to 200.
Checkout healthy for 10 minutes. Resolved in 21 minutes, fastest of the three.

postmortem.title: payments-db pool exhaustion, third time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Third pool exhaustion on payments-db (INC-019 and INC-031, now INC-042). cfg-0050 lowered max_pool_size from 200 to 90; checkout-api errors reached 8.6%.

## Impact
Checkout failed for most shoppers for about 15 minutes.

## Root cause
Kwame Mensah lowered the pool to leave connections for reconciliation-job, which also connects to payments-db. Each of the three changes had a reasonable local motive; none knew the history.

## Red herring
checkout-api v2.44.1 (dep-0333) by Mateo Silva shipped 7 minutes before the alert. The latest deploy is not the cause; the cause was two hops downstream on payments-db.

## Resolution
Priya Raman ran "Raise pool + restart payments-svc" (3 out of 3 so far).

## Follow-ups
- Reject max_pool_size below 180 in config validation.
- Give reconciliation-job its own read replica instead of payments-db connections.
postmortem.author: priya

title: Webhook backlog from one merchant's failing endpoint
summary: A large merchant's webhook endpoint started timing out; retries to it filled the delivery workers and delivery p99 for everyone reached 7,200 ms. Paused that endpoint and drained the backlog with the runbook.

timeline.text: Alert: webhooks-svc delivery p99 7,200 ms.
62% of in-flight deliveries go to one merchant endpoint that times out after 5 s. No change on webhooks-svc.
Ran 'Scale webhooks-svc and drain the delivery backlog'; paused the failing endpoint.
Backlog drained. Resolved.

postmortem.title: One slow merchant endpoint delayed everyone's webhooks
postmortem.body:
## Summary
One merchant's endpoint timed out on every delivery. Its retries took most delivery workers, and p99 for all merchants reached 7,200 ms.

## Impact
Webhooks were late for 44 minutes; none were lost.

## Root cause
Delivery workers are shared across merchants with no per-merchant concurrency limit.

## Resolution
Kai Nakamura paused the endpoint and drained the backlog with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Per-merchant concurrency limits in webhooks-svc.
postmortem.author: kai

title: Receipt emails failing again at Postmark
summary: Second Postmark outage after INC-017: 52% of sends failed for 38 minutes. Receipts were retried from kafka once it recovered.

timeline.text: Alert: notifications-svc error rate 52%.
Postmark 503s again, same as INC-017.
No fallback provider is wired up yet; wait for Postmark and let kafka buffer receipts.
Postmark recovered, backlog drained. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Postmark outage, second time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Postmark failed 52% of sends for 38 minutes, the second outage after INC-017.

## Impact
Receipts were late; none were lost.

## Root cause
External: Postmark outage. The follow-up from INC-017 (a second provider) was not done.

## Resolution
Waited for recovery; kafka buffered receipts.

## Follow-ups
- Wire SendGrid as a fallback email_provider this quarter.
postmortem.author: kai

title: ledger-db slow from table bloat; ledger-svc fell behind
summary: Autovacuum fell behind on ledger_entries after a month-end spike; ledger-db p99 reached 840 ms and ledger-svc lag 16,000 ms. Ran a manual vacuum, then replayed events the consumer had skipped on timeouts.

timeline.text: Alert: ledger-db p99 latency 840 ms.
Alert: ledger-svc event processing lag 16,000 ms.
ledger_entries has 41% dead tuples; autovacuum has not completed on it for 9 days. No recent change.
Ran VACUUM on ledger_entries with autovacuum cost limits raised.
ledger-svc skipped 312 events on statement timeouts during the slow period.
Ran 'Replay missed payment events into ledger-svc' for the skipped range.
Balances verified, lag zero. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Autovacuum could not keep up with month-end volume
postmortem.body:
## Summary
ledger_entries bloated after the month-end spike; ledger-db p99 reached 840 ms and ledger-svc fell 16,000 ms behind, skipping 312 events on timeouts.

## Impact
Merchant balances were stale for 83 minutes and 312 entries were missing until the replay.

## Root cause
Autovacuum cost limits were sized for normal days. ledger-svc skips an event on a statement timeout instead of retrying.

## Resolution
Inês Costa vacuumed by hand and replayed the skipped events with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Raise autovacuum limits for ledger_entries before month end.
- ledger-svc retries on statement timeout instead of skipping.
postmortem.author: ines

title: pricing-svc serving stale FX rates after v1.9.6
summary: dep-0377 (v1.9.6) broke the FX refresh loop; rates went stale and pricing-svc rejected 2.5% of cross-currency quotes as expired. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: pricing-svc error rate 2.5%.
FX rates have not refreshed since dep-0377; the refresh goroutine exits after its first tick.
Rolled pricing-svc back to v1.9.5.
Rates fresh, quotes succeeding. Resolved.

postmortem.title: FX refresh goroutine exited after one tick
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0377 (v1.9.6) rewrote the FX refresh loop; it returned after the first tick and rates went stale.

## Impact
2.5% of cross-currency quotes failed for 15 minutes.

## Root cause
Commit 3b7e36a by Mateo Silva: the loop returned on a nil context error.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v1.9.5.

## Follow-ups
- Alert when FX rates are older than 2 refresh intervals.
postmortem.author: mateo

title: payments-svc latency up after v3.24.7 added a second fraud call
summary: dep-0388 (v3.24.7) called fraud-svc twice per charge, before and after authorization; payments-svc p99 rose to 1,900 ms. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: payments-svc p99 latency 1,900 ms (threshold 600 ms).
Traces show two fraud-svc calls per charge since dep-0388; fraud-svc itself is within its SLO.
Rolled payments-svc back to v3.24.6.
p99 back to 310 ms. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Second fraud call doubled charge latency
postmortem.body:
## Summary
payments-svc p99 latency reached 1,900 ms for 17 minutes after dep-0388 (v3.24.7) added a post-authorization fraud score.

## Impact
Checkouts were slow; no errors.

## Root cause
Commit ec1a375 by Tomás Ortega made the second fraud call synchronous. It only feeds chargeback analytics and can run after the response.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v3.24.6.

## Follow-ups
- Send the post-authorization score through kafka instead of inline.
postmortem.author: oliver

title: api-gateway routing user calls to search-api after v2.12.0
summary: dep-0394 (v2.12.0) changed route matching order so /v1/users/* matched the search-api prefix; 2.8% of API calls returned 404. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: api-gateway error rate 2.8%.
404s from search-api for /v1/users/* paths since dep-0394.
Rolled api-gateway back to v2.11.2.
Resolved.

postmortem.title: Unordered route map broke prefix matching
postmortem.body:
## Summary
dep-0394 (v2.12.0) built the router from a map, losing route order. /v1/users/* matched the search-api route.

## Impact
2.8% of API calls failed for 13 minutes.

## Root cause
Commit 5fdaad0 by Jin Park: Go map iteration order is random, so tests passed sometimes.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v2.11.2.

## Follow-ups
- Router golden test covering every route prefix.
postmortem.author: dev

title: checkout-api 'cart not found' errors after v2.47.1
summary: dep-0409 (v2.47.1) read cart_ttl_s through a settings loader that treats durations as milliseconds; carts expired in redis-cache after 1.8 seconds and 5.2% of checkouts failed. Rolled back.

timeline.text: Alert: checkout-api error rate 5.2%.
Errors are 'cart not found'. redis-cache is healthy, but cart keys are written with a 1.8 s TTL.
dep-0409 moved cart_ttl_s to the shared settings loader, which reads durations as milliseconds.
Rolled checkout-api back to v2.47.0.
Carts persist again; error rate normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Cart TTL read in the wrong unit
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For 16 minutes 5.2% of checkouts failed with "cart not found" because dep-0409 (v2.47.1) set cart TTLs 1000 times too short.

## Impact
Shoppers who took more than two seconds between cart and payment lost their cart.

## Root cause
Commit ef1202b by Yuki Tanaka read cart_ttl_s through the shared settings loader, which assumes milliseconds unless the key ends in _ms. The key name says seconds.

## Resolution
Rolled back to v2.47.0. redis-cache was never the problem, though it showed up first in traces.

## Follow-ups
- Make the settings loader honor _s and _ms suffixes.
- Alert on cart key TTL below 60 seconds.
postmortem.author: amara

title: object-store quota reached; reconciliation could not write
summary: The settlements bucket hit its quota (98%); reconciliation-job could not write last night's results. Deleted expired report exports, raised the quota and re-ran the job.

timeline.text: Alert: object-store usage 98% of quota.
The report-exports prefix holds 3 months of exports the lifecycle rule should have expired.
Deleted expired exports and raised the bucket quota by 20%.
Re-ran reconciliation-job for last night.
Resolved.

postmortem.title: Lifecycle rule missed the report-exports prefix
postmortem.body:
## Summary
The settlements bucket filled to 98%; reconciliation-job could not write results.

## Impact
Last night's reconciliation report was 65 minutes late. No money moved.

## Root cause
The lifecycle rule (lifecycle_days) was set per prefix and report-exports was never added.

## Resolution
Dev Malhotra deleted expired exports, raised the quota and re-ran the job.

## Follow-ups
- Bucket-wide lifecycle rule with per-prefix exceptions.
postmortem.author: dev
